kanso.description: Muted-ink color family. Dark theme that invites focus, not attention.

matteblack.description: Warm, high-contrast dark theme by tahayvr.

greyscale.description: Btop grayscale ramp with koda-dark ports and deep matte-black diff washes.

nvim.note: Appearance driven since 2026-09: the light/dark pair lives in the AUTO table of nvim/lua/config/appearance.lua (dark -> kanso, light -> koda-glade) and is applied after themery, so a persisted themery pick outside the pair pins the theme (state file: stdpath('data')/themery/state.json). nvim/lua/plugins/colorscheme.lua also overrides koda's light backgrounds to #ffffff via require('koda').setup { colors = { light = ..., glade = ... } } (repo rule: light mode background is pure white), which must stay before themery.setup. To move the repo default, edit the AUTO table.

pi.note: Values are pi theme settings. greyscale uses pi's light/dark pair format (light first): greyscale-light for light terminals, greyscale for dark. Pi picks by the terminal's reported background, so it follows ghostty on its own; a single name either side pins that theme for both appearances (kanso/matte-black have no light half yet).

ghostty.note: Colors moved out of ghostty/config (inline palette/background/foreground lines there override the theme) into the light/dark pair ghostty/themes/greyscale-moshi-dark and ghostty/themes/greyscale-moshi-light, selected by `theme = dark:greyscale-moshi-dark,light:greyscale-moshi-light` so Ghostty follows the OS appearance. To switch the whole theme, add a <theme>-dark / <theme>-light pair under ghostty/themes/ and point `theme` at it. The previous inline palettes (kanso ink, kanso zenghost, matte black, greyscale ramp variants) remain in ghostty/config as commented history, and 256-color slots 52/235 (delta washes for lazygit) now live in the theme files — per appearance.

bat.note: Two greyscale themes live in bat's cache: greyscale (dark, koda-dark) and greyscale-light (light, koda-light on white). BAT_THEME wins over the --theme line in bat/config, and fish appearance_sync exports BAT_THEME=greyscale / greyscale-light from the OS appearance, so bat (and delta, which reads the same cache) flip automatically. At least one --theme line must stay uncommented as the fallback for non-fish launches. Run `bat cache --build` after editing any tmTheme.

delta.note: Appearance driven since 2026-09. [delta] activates features = greyscale; the dark half lives in [delta "greyscale"] (syntax-theme = greyscale + deep matte-black washes) and the light half in [delta "greyscale-light"] (syntax-theme = greyscale-light, pale washes, light = true). fish appearance_sync exports DELTA_FEATURES=greyscale-light in light mode, and delta applies environment features AFTER git-config features, so the light half wins without touching the file. Never pass --syntax-theme on a command line (the lazygit pager was changed to `delta --paging=never` for this reason) - a CLI value overrides both halves. To switch the repo to another theme: create <theme>{,-light}.tmTheme in delta/themes + bat/themes, point the two feature blocks at them, rebuild the bat cache, and give the light feature its own washes.

lazygit.note: lazygit 0.64 has no per-appearance theme variants, so light mode is a second config file: lazygit/greyscale-light.yml holds the koda-light gui.theme + authorColors overrides and fish appearance_sync sets LG_CONFIG_FILE=".../lazygit/config.yml,.../lazygit/greyscale-light.yml" in light mode (dark mode: LG_CONFIG_FILE=".../lazygit/config.yml"). Values for both halves are in themes/GREYSCALE.md -> "lazygit light half". The delta pager command carries no --syntax-theme so the inherited BAT_THEME/DELTA_FEATURES decide the diff colors. Non-fish launches fall back to the dark UI.

hunk.note: hunk has a large [custom_theme] block with ~40 color values and [custom_theme.syntax_scopes] with ~30 scope mappings. See themes/KANSO.md and themes/MATTEBLOCK.md for the full values. Swap the label, accent, panel, noteBorder, and all diff-color/syntax-scope values.

herdr.note: Appearance driven since 2026-09. [theme] auto_switch = true with dark_name = "catppuccin" and light_name = "catppuccin-latte"; herdr swaps the base theme on the host terminal's light/dark notification and layers [theme.custom] (shared values, dark era) plus [theme.custom.light] on top. To switch the repo theme, rewrite the shared [theme.custom] block and give [theme.custom.light] a matching light half (see themes/GREYSCALE.md -> 'herdr light block'); the kanso and matte-black values stay commented in place. Validate with `herdr config check`. Old behaviour: a single hardcoded [theme.custom] block, no appearance switching.

starship.note: Colors are ANSI slot names since 2026-09 (red 1 status/error, bright-cyan 14 success/time, purple 5 directory/bun, bright-yellow 11 branch/zig, white 7 neutral wrapper), so the prompt follows the terminal palette and flips with ghostty's light/dark pair — no per-theme edit needed. Fixed hexes and the truecolor escapes in the (disabled) custom.git_changes awk script were removed because they were invisible on light backgrounds (#8ebeec 2.0:1, #ff7676 2.7:1 on white). Switching to a theme with a different ANSI palette needs no change here; only reintroducing a hex would break light/dark following.

moshi.note: Moshi (iOS terminal) requires manual import: Settings → Theme → Import theme → paste contents of moshi/<theme>-theme.json

appearance.note: Tools that follow the OS light/dark appearance, and how. bat/delta/lazygit follow only inside fish shells (the env vars come from fish/functions/appearance_sync.fish); elsewhere they fall back to their dark halves. dark_only tools are single-theme until they get a light half. The bat/delta theme names and the lazygit override file are hardcoded in fish/functions/appearance_sync.fish — update them there when switching the repo theme, together with the [delta "…"] feature blocks and lazygit's light override file.

follows.nvim: config/appearance.lua AUTO pair: dark kanso / light koda-glade, polled + FocusGained
follows.pi: settings.json theme "<light>/<dark>" pair; pi reads the terminal background
follows.starship: ANSI slot names only (red/bright-cyan/purple/bright-yellow/white), so the prompt inherits the active ghostty half
follows.delta: DELTA_FEATURES=greyscale-light (fish appearance_sync) overrides the [delta "greyscale"] feature; no --syntax-theme on any command line
follows.bat: BAT_THEME=greyscale-light from fish appearance_sync; bat/config --theme stays as the fallback
follows.lazygit: LG_CONFIG_FILE adds lazygit/greyscale-light.yml in light mode (own UI) + inherited delta env

appearance.repo_rule: Light mode: every main background (panel, sidebar, surfaces, panes, tab bar, terminal) is pure white #ffffff. The only non-white colors are diff boxes (add/remove/change washes) and selection highlights (selected tab/workspace/agent row, cursor row, text selection, borders). Upstream koda light backgrounds (#faf9f5, glade #f7f7f7) are overridden in the ports, never patched in the koda.nvim submodule.
